newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia nuclear workers to stage protest - agency.
newsitem.headline: Russia nuclear workers to stage protest - agency.

text.p: Dozens of angry nuclear power station workers are preparing to march to Moscow to demand the government pays wage arrears dating back four months, Interfax news agency said on Wednesday.

Interfax quoted a deputy trade union leader, Vladimir Kashkin, as saying the organisers of the 350-km (220-mile) protest march from the Smolensk plant expected workers of Russia's other eight stations to join in.

Another deputy union leader, Ivan Gradobitov, told Interfax the protesters wanted to meet Nuclear Energy Minister Viktor Mikhailov to demand money and warn him that poor financing could harm security of the potentially dangerous sector.
The march, involving about 150 workers, is scheduled to start on Thursday.

Kashkin said the government's debt to nuclear sector workers amounted to 250 billion roubles ($43.5 million). The two biggest nuclear centres alone -- Arzamas 16 and Chelyabinsk 70 -- were owed 73 billion roubles ($12.7 million).
The nuclear sector -- long the pride of Soviet science and used to preferential treatment -- is experiencing financial crisis. Most of its underpaied workers have not received any money for months.
On Tuesday, workers in the Russian Far East at a base servicing Pacific Fleet nuclear submarines briefly blocked the Trans-Siberian railway in a protest against wage delays.

Gradobitov said workers at Arzamas 16, where a researcher recently died after a radiation accident, were planning to advise President Boris Yeltsin that poor financing could lead to more nuclear accidents.

Arzamas-16 researcher Alexander Zakharov had been conducting a weapons test last month involving a controlled nuclear chain reaction using small amounts of uranium when what officials called "a serious breach of the rules" caused an "irregular radiation situation involving the emission of neutron rays".
Zakharov died in a Moscow hospital several days later.
